blocks.orig: Tanzania yellow fever requirements can sometimes seem confusing, but we’re here to help! As a yellow fever-free country, Tanzania is safe to travel when it comes to steering clear of this virus. On this page, we answer all your questions on the yellow fever virus and whether a yellow fever vaccine is required for Tanzania.
blocks.html: The yellow fever rules for Tanzania can look a little confusing at times, but we’re happy to help! Tanzania is a yellow fever-free country, so when it comes to avoiding this virus it is a safe place to travel. Below you’ll find answers to all your questions about the yellow fever virus and whether you need a yellow fever vaccine for Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Tanzania?
blocks.html: Is a yellow fever vaccination required for Tanzania?

blocks.orig: Great news: for the vast majority of travellers to this beautiful country, you do not need this vaccine! According to the World Health Organization’s classification, Tanzania currently poses a low risk of yellow fever. If you reside in a country with no risk of yellow fever, then you do not need the yellow fever vaccine as part of your necessary travel vaccinations.
blocks.html: Good news: if you are like most travellers to this beautiful country, this vaccine isn’t required for you! Under the World Health Organization’s classification, the risk of yellow fever in Tanzania is currently low. If you live in a country where there is no yellow fever risk, the yellow fever vaccine is not one of the travel vaccinations you need.

blocks.orig: Yellow fever is a viral disease spread through mosquito bites. Symptoms of yellow fever typically take 3 to 6 days to develop and can include fever, chills, headache and muscle aches. Yellow Fever is serious, with around 15% of people who get yellow fever develop a serious or life-threatening illness.
blocks.html: Yellow fever is a virus spread by mosquito bites. It usually takes 3 to 6 days for symptoms to appear, and they can include headache, chills, fever and muscle aches. It is a serious disease: about 15% of people who catch yellow fever go on to develop a serious or life-threatening illness.

blocks.orig: Proof of yellow fever vaccination is only required upon arrival if you are travelling from a country with a risk of the virus. This list currently does not include any country in Europe and the United States. (View the full list of Yellow Fever high-risk countries).
blocks.html: You only have to show proof of yellow fever vaccination on arrival if you are coming from a country where the virus is a risk. At present, that list does not include the United States or any European country. (See the complete list of high-risk Yellow Fever countries).

blocks.orig: An important note, however. If you’re transiting through one of the yellow fever high-risk countries for a period of 12 hours or more, you will be required to receive the yellow fever vaccination. If this is the case on your trip to Tanzania, we strongly advise seeing your doctor and checking your Tanzania vaccination requirements with a healthcare professional before travelling.
blocks.html: There is one important exception, though. If you transit through a yellow fever high-risk country for 12 hours or longer, you must have the yellow fever vaccination. If that applies to your trip to Tanzania, we strongly recommend that you see your doctor and confirm your Tanzania vaccination requirements with a healthcare professional before you go.

blocks.orig: The yellow fever vaccination is given as a single dose and should be administered at least 10 days before entering a high-risk yellow fever country. A single dose is capable of providing life protection against the yellow fever virus so make sure you receive proof of vaccination from your doctor or health professional. If you are required to receive a yellow fever vaccine before travelling, you will also need to show your proof of vaccination upon arrival in Tanzania.
blocks.html: You receive the yellow fever vaccination as one single dose, and it should be given no later than 10 days before you enter a high-risk yellow fever country. One dose can give you lifelong protection against the yellow fever virus, so be sure to get proof of vaccination from your doctor or health professional. If you do need the yellow fever vaccine before your trip, you will also have to show that proof when you arrive in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Should your doctor recommend against the vaccine due to underlying health issues or other health-related factors, you can still travel to Tanzania with an official letter from the doctor. Showing it to the immigration officer upon arrival would waive the requirement, and your trip will go on as planned.
blocks.html: If your doctor advises against the vaccine because of underlying health conditions or other medical reasons, you can still travel to Tanzania with an official doctor’s letter. Show it to the immigration officer when you arrive and the requirement is waived, so your trip can continue as planned.
